prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

[P3] source: https://digitalagencynetwork.com/lululemon-advertising-marketing/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2024 | published: unknown
"2. How does Lululemon advertise its products? Honestly, Lululemon’s advertising is far more subtle than most people realize. [P4] source: https://digitalagencynetwork.com/lululemon-advertising-marketing/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Ambassador Program of Lululemon The local ambassador program is, in digital marketing terms, a micro-influencer strategy implemented at massive scale before “micro-influencer strategy” was even a concept. This creates an army of credible, hyperlocal brand advocates who post from their own authentic contexts."

[P5] source: https://www.companieshistory.com/lululemon-target-market/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2025 | published: unknown
"How Lululemon Reaches Its Audience Lululemon reaches its audience through a mix that leans heavily on physical presence and community rather than mass advertising. The company ended fiscal 2025 with 811 company-operated stores, adding 44 net new locations during the year. Stores host free yoga classes, run clubs, and in-store events, turning retail into a regular meeting place rather than a one-time visit. The ambassador program is the marketing spine. More than 4,000 local store ambassadors, mostly yoga instructors, trainers, and run coaches, anchor each market with classes and social posts."

[P6] source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbeseq/2021/08/31/what-lululemons-latest-campaign-tells-us-about-loyalty/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2022, Aug 31, 2021 | published: unknown

[P7] source: https://exposureninja.com/blog/lululemon-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Community The community tab on the lululemon website is where they house all their interactive content including workouts, info about their ambassadors, events, goal setting, and lululemon’s impact statements. It has content that caters to all sides of its audience, from yogis to runners. There are blogs, videos, training guides and even workout playlists. lululemon’s online studio has a wealth of content based around a variety of workouts and promoting their visitors to use #thesweatlife if they are sharing their workout journey on social media."

[P8] source: https://digitalagencynetwork.com/lululemon-advertising-marketing/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Third, it generates brand-consistent user-generated content that no paid campaign could replicate. ## Real Lululemon Advertising Campaigns One of the most underrated aspects of Lululemon marketing is the quality of its advertising skills! While the brand isn’t doing Super Bowl spots, the campaigns they do produce are consistently creative, emotionally resonant, and strategically aligned with their brand values. Let’s look at four that stand out."

[P9] source: https://corporate.lululemon.com/about-us | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"We are a purpose-driven brand and our values guide us in all that we do – from our business ## strategy and innovation, to how we connect and build our strong culture. Our Purpose, Mission & Values Inclusion for All"

[P10] source: https://exposureninja.com/blog/lululemon-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"They have professionally shot imagery alongside user-generated content and they are making use of all Instagram’s features, including the all-important Reels. Professional Image on lululemon's instagram User generated content on lululemon's instagram lululemon's Instagram reels Judging by the jumps in engagement on the posts, it’s likely lululemon has been putting money behind some posts that have performed well or that are speaking about a new product launch or a campaign. Going back to the user-generated content, lululemon has given itself a great foundation to work from by encouraging customers to use #thesweatlife in their posts about lululemon."
